title: Clovey Restaurant
summary: A warm, fast, mobile-first website for a modern restaurant - menu, story, and reservations in one effortless experience.
body:
Clovey needed a website that felt as considered as the food. We designed and built a brand-forward, mobile-first site that puts the menu, the story, and the booking flow within a tap of each other.

The build is fast by default - optimised images, clean semantic markup, and search-friendly structure so the restaurant ranks for the searches that matter locally. Reservations and contact are friction-free on a phone, where most diners actually decide.

The result is a site that loads quickly, reads beautifully, and turns a casual visit into a booking.
challenge: Clovey needed a website as considered as the food - and one that worked where diners actually decide: on a phone. The brand deserved better than a slow, generic template that was painful to update.
approach: We designed a brand-forward, mobile-first experience that puts the menu, the story, and the booking flow a tap apart. The build is fast by default - optimised images, clean semantic markup, and a search-friendly structure - and fully editable without a developer.
outcome: A site that loads quickly, reads beautifully, and turns a casual visit into a booking. Menus and hours update in seconds, and the structure is built to rank for the local searches that fill tables.
seoTitle: Clovey Restaurant - Restaurant Website Case Study
seoDescription: How we designed and built a fast, brand-forward, mobile-first website for Clovey Restaurant - menu, story, and bookings.

title: FitPlanCoach
summary: A production-grade fitness web app that turns coaching plans into a clean, guided experience for clients.
body:
FitPlanCoach is a web application built to make coaching scalable. We designed and engineered a clear, guided product where plans, progress, and day-to-day actions live in one place.

Under the hood it's a modern, type-safe stack built to grow - fast page loads, a responsive interface that works on the gym floor, and an architecture ready for new features without a rewrite. The interface stays out of the way so the training does the talking.

From UI to backend, it was delivered end to end by one person.
challenge: FitPlanCoach needed to make coaching scalable - turning plans, progress, and daily actions into one clear product instead of spreadsheets and scattered messages.
approach: We designed and engineered a guided web app on a modern, type-safe stack: fast page loads, a responsive interface that works on the gym floor, and an architecture ready for new features without a rewrite.
outcome: A production-grade product that feels effortless for clients and was delivered end to end, from UI to backend, and ready to grow.
seoTitle: FitPlanCoach - Fitness Web App Case Study
seoDescription: How we designed and built FitPlanCoach, a production-grade fitness web app, end to end on a modern stack.

title: Banafee Group
summary: A bilingual corporate site for a Malaysian halal food and retail group, built as one cinematic scroll with its own markdown blog and self-hosted admin.
body:
Banafee Group has run halal food and retail in Malaysia since 1970, trading today as Banafee Xpress and Banafee Mart. The brief was a corporate site that carried that heritage without reading like a brochure, and that the team could keep updating themselves.

The result is a single-page experience built around momentum scrolling and scroll-triggered reveals: parallax section headers, animated counters, a pinned horizontal gallery that walks through twelve outlet and investment formats, and a custom cursor in the brand gold. Every section was written by hand in both English and Bahasa Melayu, with machine translation available for further languages.

Behind it sits a markdown blog and a password-protected admin with a live-preview editor and image upload, so news and openings go up without a developer. Structured data, sitemap, manifest and security headers were part of the build rather than an afterthought.
challenge: A group with more than fifty years of trading history needed a site that felt considered rather than templated, served customers in two languages, and could be updated by the team without going back to a developer for every announcement.
approach: One cinematic scroll built on momentum scrolling and scroll-triggered reveals, with a pinned horizontal gallery for the twelve outlet formats and animated counters for the group's numbers. Both language versions were hand-written rather than machine-translated. A markdown blog and a password-protected admin with live preview and image upload put publishing in the client's hands.
outcome: A bilingual corporate site the group owns and edits themselves, with structured data, sitemap and manifest for search, and hardened admin sessions, rate-limited login and security headers on the private side. Measured with Google PageSpeed Insights on 3 August 2026: SEO 100 out of 100, cumulative layout shift of 0.018 against Google's 0.1 threshold, and a desktop largest contentful paint of 1.1 seconds. These are lab measurements rather than field data, and anyone can rerun them.
seoTitle: Banafee Group - Corporate Website Case Study
seoDescription: How we designed and built a bilingual corporate site for Banafee Group, a Malaysian halal food and retail group, with a self-hosted blog and admin.
